instagram_reel.script:
If you think all rosé tastes light and breezy, let me introduce you to Tavel. It’s from the southern Rhône in France, and it’s the only AOC there made only for rosé.

That matters, because this wine has real colour, real texture, and a savoury edge that makes it a proper food wine. You’ll find red berries, stone fruit, maybe a little almond, and it can absolutely hold its own at the table.

And yes, I’d pour this with jerk chicken, curried goat, pelau, or oxtail stew. That herb-and-spice energy just works.

If you want a rosé with a little more presence, Tavel is the one to know.

linkedin.post:
Tavel is a useful reminder that rosé can be a serious wine category with real breadth.

Located in the southern Rhône, just across from Châteauneuf-du-Pape, Tavel is the only AOC in France dedicated exclusively to rosé. That singular focus, along with a long winemaking history and a blend-driven approach, gives the wines more structure and depth than many people expect from rosé.

For trade and hospitality, that matters. Tavel is built for the table. Its savoury backbone, berry fruit, and food-friendly texture make it an easy recommendation for guests looking for a rosé with more presence.

It also opens the door to pairings that go beyond the usual summer shorthand. Tavel works beautifully with herb-forward, spice-forward dishes, including Caribbean food such as jerk chicken, curried goat, pelau, and oxtail stew.

If you’re looking for a rosé that can do more, Tavel belongs on the shortlist.
